Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 98, verse 1–5:

(p-315) Surat al-Bayyinah

It is Meccan according to the view of Yahya ibn Salam, but according to the majority it is Medinan, and this is the correct view.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist﴾. Its meaning: those who disbelieved among the Jews and Christians, who are the People of the Book, and the polytheists, who are the worshippers of idols among the Arabs, and others who have no book, were not going to desist.

﴿Munfakkin﴾ (desisting) has four interpretations. The first: they were not going to cease from polytheism ﴿until there came to them clear evidence﴾, until the truth became clear to them.

This is a second view: they continued to persist in polytheism and doubt until there came to them clear evidence, meaning the messengers. This was said by al-Rabi'.

The third: they did not separate and did not differ, in that God would send to them a messenger, until God sent Muhammad (ﷺ), and then they separated, so some of them believed in their Lord and some of them disbelieved. This was said by Ibn 'Isa.

The fourth: they were not to be left unseparated from the proofs of God the Exalted, until there came to them the clear evidence by which the proof is established against them. Imru' al-Qays said:

؎ When I say, "I will disengage from her love," the one clinging to love refuses except to cling to it.

(p-316)

As for ﴿al-bayyinah﴾ (the clear evidence) here, there are three aspects:

The first: the Qur'an. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: the Messenger in whom the signs of prophethood are manifest.

The third: the clarification of the truth and the manifestation of proofs.

In the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not [going to desist]﴾, and in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿The polytheists and the People of the Book were not going to desist﴾.

﴿A messenger from God﴾, meaning Muhammad.

﴿Reciting purified scriptures﴾, meaning the Qur'an.

It may also mean, secondly: he follows, with his prophethood, the revelation of the purified scriptures upon the prophets before him.

As for ﴿purified﴾ there are two aspects:

One: purified from polytheism. This was said by Ikrimah.

The second: purified in its judgments, through good mention and praise. This was said by Qatadah.

It may also mean, thirdly: because of their descent from God.

﴿Therein are upright books﴾. Regarding this there are two aspects:

One: meaning the upright books of God, which the Qur'an mentioned and whose truthfulness was established in it. This was related by Ibn 'Isa.

The second: meaning the just obligations of God. This was said by al-Suddi.

﴿And those who were given the Book did not divide except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾, meaning the Jews and Christians.

﴿Except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾. Regarding this there are two views:

One: the Qur'an. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah.

The second: Muhammad (ﷺ). This was said by Ibn Shajarah.

It may also mean, thirdly: the clear evidence is what is in their books of the authenticity of his prophethood.

﴿And they were commanded only to worship God, making the religion sincerely His﴾. Regarding this there are three aspects:

One: affirming to Him worship.

The second: intending in their hearts the countenance of God the Exalted in their worship.

The third: when one says, "There is no god but God," to say immediately after it, "Praise be to God." This was said by Ibn Jarir.(p-317)

It may also mean, fourthly: except that they make their religion sincere in affirming his prophethood.

﴿Hunafa'﴾ (upright in faith). Regarding this there are six aspects:

One: followers.

The second: upright, said by Muhammad ibn Ka'b.

The third: sincere, said by Khasif.

The fourth: Muslims, said by al-Dahhak. And the poet said:

؎ O caliph of the Merciful, we are a people who are upright in faith, prostrating morning and evening.

The fifth: meaning pilgrims. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ata' al-'Awfi said: when "hanif" and "muslim" are combined, the meaning of "hanif" is the pilgrim, and when "hanif" stands alone, its meaning is Muslim. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the Arabs do not call anyone "hanif" except one who has performed the pilgrimage and been circumcised.

The sixth: that they are believers in all the messengers. This was said by Abu Qilabah.

﴿And establish prayer and give zakah, and that is the upright religion﴾. Regarding this there are three aspects:

One: its meaning is that this is the religion of the upright community.

The second: that is the religion of the upright judgment. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The third: that is the clear reckoning. This was said by Muqatil.

It may also mean, fourthly: that is the religion of one who stands for God with His right.
